intended_object: The homomorphism K₀(F) : K₀(C, E) → K₀(D, E') induced by an exact functor F between (essentially small) Quillen exact categories, sending [X] to [F X]. This comes from the docstring and module documentation (Weibel, K-book II.7).
explanation: `ExactK0 E` is built as a quotient: the free abelian group on isomorphism-class codes of objects, modulo the subgroup generated by the relations [X₂] − [X₁] − [X₃], one for each conflation. `PresentedK0.map` is `QuotientAddGroup.map` applied to `freeMap F`, the map on generators sending [X] to [F X]. The well-definedness condition is that F sends each relation into the closure of the target relations. `mapsTo_exactRelations` establishes this condition from `IsConflationExact`, which says that F (an additive functor) carries E-conflations to E'-conflations. That is the standard notion of an exact functor between exact categories, and the lemma `map_of` confirms that the map sends [X] to [F X]. So this is exactly the textbook induced map on K₀. The setting is the natural one: additive categories with an exact structure and additive exact functors, with essential smallness needed for K₀ to exist. Mathlib has no exact-category K₀, so there is no more general counterpart.
